 Fuel & Fertilizer Price Tracker: Nov. 12, 2026 
 Farm News Media 
 November 12, 2026 
 Farm News Media 
 The national average price of highway diesel fuel has continued setting new records on a daily basis since Labor Day, according to the Energy Information Administration (EIA), surpassing the previous record of $5.82 per gallon set in 2022.
 As of Sept. 21, the national average price of diesel had hit at $6.490 per gallon, according to Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy, with Michigan experiencing  some of the nation’s highest spikes in gas and diesel prices.
 According to Grand Rapids-based fuel distributor Crystal Flash, Michigan highway diesel hit $6.71, while off-road dyed diesel was priced at $5.95 per gallon for Sept. 21 delivery — an increase of nearly 96% over the last six months — and an even larger increase of 156.5% since January 3, when priced at $2.32 per gallon.
 With U.S. inventory levels of diesel reaching a 30-year low of just 25 days coverage as expected demand grows going into fall harvest and the start of the home heating season, industry experts predict the nation’s national average price for diesel shows no signs of slowing.
 De Haan said escalation of geopolitical tensions on multiple fronts between the U.S. and Iran, new hostilities in the Red Sea, and the shutdown of Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline have combined to “jolt prices sharply higher.”
 Two additional Russian refineries were also knocked offline following recent Ukrainian drone attacks, straining global refined product supplies even further, making any potential price relief very unlikely.
 “Diesel prices could climb even faster in the wake of the new refinery attacks. While most of the country transitions to cheaper winter-blend gasoline this week, the scale of ongoing geopolitical escalations makes meaningful price relief unlikely in the near term,” De Haan said, suggesting continued price volatility.
 Charles Kennedy with oilprice.com reported that Russia announced it will extend the ban on all diesel exports that was originally due to expire September 30, to October 31, citing delayed refinery maintenance and the need to rebuild three of its six largest refineries following Ukrainian drone attacks.
 Russia, once the world’s largest exporter of refined oil products, has now been forced to import fuels, with imports surging to a record 172,000 tonnes in August — more than seven times the previous monthly high, according to the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air.
 While U.S. refiners are producing an estimated 3.5 million barrels per day to meet domestic diesel demand, they’re also capitalizing on strong global demand, according to the EIA, with record diesel export levels as high as 1.9 million barrels per day.
 Below you will find fuel pricing information updated daily and benchmarked against prices as of Feb. 27, 2026, provided by Crystal Flash .
 Similarly, you’ll find updated fertilizer pricing information updated as needed and provided by Michigan Agricultural Commodities to assist producers as they monitor price impacts.
